short.q: Describe how a persistent cookie could be used by an online shop.
short.model: A persistent cookie is stored on the customer's drive after they leave. The shop can use it to remember login details or preferences, or to show adverts based on pages they viewed.
points: Stored on the device after the browser closes
Used for targeted advertising (any one use)

short.q: Explain why public Wi-Fi puts a user at risk of data interception and how HTTPS helps.
short.model: On public Wi-Fi a hacker can use a packet sniffer to capture packets travelling across the network. HTTPS encrypts the data so the captured packets cannot be understood.

short.q: Describe two differences between phishing and pharming.
short.model: Phishing uses an email or message that the user must respond to by clicking a link. Pharming installs malicious code that redirects the user to a fake website automatically, even if the correct address is typed.
points: Phishing needs the user to click a link in a message
Pharming redirects automatically using malicious code
Pharming works even when the correct URL is typed

short.q: Explain why a blockchain is difficult to tamper with.
short.model: Each block contains the hash of the block before it. If someone changes a block, its hash changes and no longer matches the next block, breaking the chain. The ledger is also copied on many computers, so the change would be spotted.
points: Each block stores previous block's hash
Changing one block changes its hash and breaks the chain
Ledger copied on many computers / change detected

short.q: Describe how an automated greenhouse keeps the temperature at 20 °C.
short.model: A temperature sensor sends readings to a microprocessor. The microprocessor compares the reading with 20 °C. If it is too cold it signals an actuator to switch on the heater; if too hot it opens the windows. The sensor keeps reading in a loop.
